title: Vanishing for sheaves supported on closed points
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$. Let $F$ be an
abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose support
is contained in the set of
closed points of $X$. Then
$H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0$ for $q>0$. (*Source:* Stacks Project,
Tag [0F1F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1F), first
assertion.)

proof.text: The structure map of X is locally of finite type over Spec K, so X is locally Noetherian by Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian. Its quasi-compactness gives CompactSpace X by QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace. The locally Noetherian instance supplies QuasiSeparatedSpace X. These are the hypotheses for the cohomology-colimit theorem.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion

proof.text: Apply closedPointSheaf_filteredColimit_finiteSupport to F. It gives the filtered category of finitely generated subobjects, a colimit cocone c with c.pt isomorphic to F, and, for each subobject G, finite closed-point support S, a reduced closed immersion i with range S, and G isomorphic to i_* i^* G. No choice of a new geometric object from an unproved mere existence statement is made: these existential witnesses are eliminated only in the proof.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion

proof.text: For a finitely generated subobject G, take U to be the open complement of S. The range of the closed immersion i is closed, so U is open. Its range is disjoint from the range of i. Vanishing of U^* i_* and the supplied isomorphism for G show U^* G = 0. The complement of U is S, hence finite; every point in it is closed. The closed-point residue-field theorem makes every such residue field separably closed. Apply the already proved source-library subsingleton_H_of_isZero_upperStar to obtain Subsingleton (Sheaf.H G (n+1)). This packages the finite point decomposition, pointwise vanishing, and exact finite direct image of the original steps without reconstructing a finite reduced scheme.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion

proof.text: Write the positive degree q as n+1. Apply the arbitrary-index-category abelian form of filtered-colimit cohomology, Scheme.H_map_isColimit_of_isFiltered_of_large. Every cohomology class of c.pt is the image of a class of one finitely generated subobject. That class is zero by the preceding step, and its image is zero. Thus Sheaf.H c.pt (n+1) is a subsingleton. Transport across c.pt isomorphic to F using Sheaf.functorH to obtain Subsingleton (Sheaf.H F (n+1)). No smallness bound on the full category of subobjects is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion

proof.text: Let Gamma be abelian global sections. The source-library homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso identifies H^q(RGamma(F[0])) with (Gamma.rightDerived q).obj F, using plus/unbounded compatibility and the single-object derived comparison. On the other hand extSectionsIso identifies Sheaf.H F q with the homology of Gamma applied to the chosen injective resolution; isoRightDerivedObjCochainComplex identifies this with (Gamma.rightDerived q).obj F. Compose these explicit isomorphisms and transport the zero-object property from the subsingleton abelian cohomology group. This is exactly the unbounded derived cohomology object in the unchanged statement.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$. Let $F$ be an
abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose support
is contained in the set of
closed points of $X$. Then
$H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0$ for $q>0$.

proof.text:
The scheme $X$ is Noetherian because it is of finite type over a
field. The set of closed points is closed under specialization, and
the support of $F$ is contained in it, so the approximation
[lem-kun-cp-approximation] writes $F=\varinjlim_iF_i$ as a
filtered colimit of finitely generated subsheaves $F_i$, the support
of each $F_i$ being a finite set $Z_i$ of closed points of $X$.
Give $Z_i$ its reduced
closed subscheme structure and write $i:Z_i\to X$ for the closed
immersion. By [lem-kun-04ca] the sheaf $F_i$ is of the form
$i_*\mathcal G_i$ for a sheaf $\mathcal G_i$ on
$(Z_i)_{\Et}$, and by [lem-kun-closed-point-field] every
closed point of $X$ has a residue field which is a finite, purely
inseparable, hence separably closed extension of $K$; so $Z_i$ is
a finite disjoint union of spectra of separably closed fields.
By [lem-kun-03qu-sep-closed] (on each component, with
$H^q$ of a disjoint union being the direct sum of the $H^q$ of the
components) we get $H^q((Z_i)_{\Et},\mathcal G_i)=0$ for $q>0$.
Since $i$ is finite,
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and
[lem-kun-leray-bdd] (or [lem-kun-leray-finite]) give
$H^q(X_{\Et},F_i)=H^q((Z_i)_{\Et},\mathcal G_i)=0$ for $q>0$.
Finally, the higher-direct-image limit formula
[sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-limit] of the smooth-base-change chapter, applied to the
constant inverse system $X_i=X$ with the compatible system of sheaves
$F_i$, shows that cohomology commutes with the filtered colimit:
$H^q(X_{\Et},F)=\varinjlim_iH^q(X_{\Et},F_i)=0$ for $q>0$.
